topic: Displaced extra-articular Colles-pattern distal radius fracture

display.title: The Fall That Injured a Wrist
display.subtitle: A fall in the kitchen. A painful deformed wrist. Protect function without unnecessary tests.

patient.name: Margaret Wilson
patient.presenting_event: Slipped on wet kitchen tiles and landed on the extended right hand about 90 minutes ago.

history.chief_complaint: Right wrist pain and deformity, pain 8/10.
history.mechanism: Low-energy fall onto an outstretched right hand; no direct elbow impact.
positive: Unable to hold a cup in the right hand
negative: No head injury or loss of consciousness
No finger numbness or other injuries
history.goal: Return to independent cooking and gardening

inspection: Closed swollen wrist with dorsal contour change
No skin tenting or open wound
palpation: No snuffbox, ulnar shaft, elbow or hand tenderness
neurovascular: Radial pulse present, warm fingers, capillary refill <2 s
Intact median, ulnar and radial sensory examination
Thumb opposition, finger abduction and finger extension intact
safety_red_flags: Pain out of proportion or excessive pain on passive finger stretch

learning_objective: Select focused imaging, recognize dorsal displacement, sequence safe closed reduction, document reassessment and arrange secondary prevention.

options.label: Apply a tight circumferential cast immediately
options.teaching_point: A tight cast may threaten circulation as swelling increases.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: A tight cast may threaten circulation as swelling increases.

options.label: Advise free-finger, elbow and shoulder movement and arrange falls/osteoporosis assessment
options.teaching_point: Maintain uninvolved joint mobility and prevent future fragility fractures.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Maintain uninvolved joint mobility and prevent future fragility fractures.

options.label: Perform gentle closed reduction by appropriately trained clinician
options.teaching_point: Restore alignment while protecting skin, nerves and vessels.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Restore alignment while protecting skin, nerves and vessels.

options.label: Use extreme palmar-flexion casting
options.teaching_point: Extreme flexion is not recommended.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Extreme flexion is not recommended.

options.label: Apply a well-molded below-elbow splint/cast in near-neutral wrist position, allowing for swelling
options.teaching_point: A supported position avoids extreme palmar flexion.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. A supported position avoids extreme palmar flexion.

options.label: Consent and arrange clinician-performed appropriate regional anesthesia for reduction
options.teaching_point: A trained practitioner should provide appropriate pain control and reduction.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. A trained practitioner should provide appropriate pain control and reduction.

options.label: Give routine prophylactic antibiotics for this closed injury

options.when_selected_mentor: Think again: No indication in uncomplicated closed fracture.

options.when_selected_mentor: Think again: Plain wrist radiographs are first-line.

options.label: Document skin status, circulation and median/ulnar/radial nerve function before intervention

options.label: Review radiographs, discuss reduction and nonoperative versus surgical indications with the orthopedic team

options.label: Review post-reduction PA/lateral radiograph report and decide if alignment is acceptable

options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Never assume an adequate reduction without confirmation.

options.label: Obtain weekly radiographs for all patients regardless of findings
options.teaching_point: Serial imaging should be clinically targeted.
options.when_selected_mentor: Think again: Serial imaging should be clinically targeted.

stage_messages.history: Good questions uncover the mechanism and red flags. You do not need to ask everything—ask what changes your decisions.
stage_messages.examination: Slow and safe. Inspect first, localize tenderness and protect injured structures while checking nerves and circulation.
stage_messages.investigations: Choose the smallest clinically sufficient set of tests. I’ll show you each written report as you order it.
stage_messages.diagnosis: Now connect the mechanism, examination and investigations. Which diagnosis actually explains all three?

stage_messages.knowledge_check: Nice work! Three quick questions to lock in the clinical reasoning.
stage_messages.completion: Great job with Margaret! The best clinicians are careful about both decisions and patient safety.

questions.question: Which radiographic feature distinguishes Colles from Smith?
questions.explanation: Colles denotes dorsal, Smith volar displacement/angulation.

questions.question: What must be documented both before and after reduction?
questions.explanation: Repeat sensory, motor and perfusion checks detect complications.

questions.question: Is routine surgery superior long-term for every older adult with a displaced distal radius fracture?

options.text: Only if there is no pain

questions.explanation: AAOS/ASSH evidence does not show improved long-term outcomes with routine fixation in geriatric patients.
